name: How long does commercial construction take from permit to completion?

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical commercial construction project take from permit approval to final completion?
mainEntity.text: How long does a typical commercial construction project take from permit approval to final completion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Construction duration depends on project size, complexity, and how much of the building must be upgraded behind the walls. A small tenant improvement can finish in a few months once the permit is issued, but larger renovations, restaurant build-outs, or new commercial buildings can take much longer. The schedule is often driven less by visible framing and more by coordination items such as submittals, inspections, utility connections, long-lead equipment, and city review cycles. Projects in Los Angeles-area cities also face potential delays from correction comments, traffic control requirements, or older-building surprises. A realistic schedule should include preconstruction design time, permit processing, procurement, field work, punch list, and final sign-off. Owners should also plan for buffer time before lease start dates, opening dates, or financing milestones.
acceptedAnswer.description: Small commercial remodels may finish in a few months after permits are issued, while larger build-outs or new buildings can take a year or longer. The biggest schedule drivers are permit delays, utility work, inspections, and long-lead materials.
